title: Restricted PBW basis and top coefficient pairing for a Borel radical
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq G$, with $B$ a Borel subgroup and $U=R_u(B)$ its unipotent radical, and character lattice $X=X^*(T)$ and positive roots $\Psi^+$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Here split means a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$, Borel means maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup, and unipotent radical means the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. Choose an ordering $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N$ of $\Psi^+$ and root parametrizations $x_{\beta_i}:\mathbf G_a\simeq U_{\beta_i}$ [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Put $e_i=(dx_{\beta_i})_0(1)\in\mathfrak u=\operatorname{Lie}(U)$, the tangent Lie algebra, with restricted operation $x^{[p]}$ given by the $p$th iterate of its invariant derivation. Define $A=u(\mathfrak u)$ as the quotient of the tensor algebra by $xy-yx-[x,y]$ and $x^p-x^{[p]}$. Conjugation by $T$ acts on $A$; a weight $\gamma\in X$ means the character identity $ta=\gamma(t)a$ after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Then the ordered monomials
$$e_1^{a_1}\cdots e_N^{a_N}\quad(0\leq a_i<p)$$
form an $F$-basis of $A$ and are weight vectors of weight $\sum_i a_i\beta_i$. Put $z=e_1^{p-1}\cdots e_N^{p-1}$, and let $L:A\to F$ take the coefficient of $z$ in this basis. The bilinear pairing $(a,b)\mapsto L(ab)$ is nondegenerate in both arguments. The weight space of weight $\tau=(p-1)\sum_i\beta_i$ is exactly $Fz$, and $L$ is zero on every other weight space. For $N=0$ these statements mean $A=F$, $z=1$, and $L=\operatorname{id}_F$.

source.place: Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.3, printed p.149, applied to a Borel unipotent radical; root coordinates in Milne 21.68 and 21.84. WANTED: Mathieu is not stored locally; read online at https://www.imsc.res.in/~knr/vdk/mathieu.pdf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] to the given reductive Borel pair and the chosen order of all its positive roots. Composing its scheme isomorphism with the parametrizations $x_{\beta_i}$ and taking tangent vectors at the identity gives an isomorphism $F^N\to\mathfrak u$ sending the $i$th standard vector to $e_i$: on dual numbers, multiplication of tangent vectors is addition. Thus the $e_i$ form an ordered basis. Apply [lem-sfb-restricted-rational-differentiation] to the smooth affine finite-type group $U$; its invariant-derivation operation makes this tangent Lie algebra a restricted Lie algebra with exactly the operation in the statement.

source.place: Theorem 21.68(a), p.445; invariant derivations, 10.29 and the paragraph before 11.36, pp.195--196 and 223.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-restricted-pbw-basis] now hold for $L=\mathfrak u$ with this ordered basis; its tensor quotient is precisely $A$. It gives the asserted basis. The conjugation formula in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], evaluated on dual numbers over an arbitrary commutative $F$-algebra $R$, gives $t e_i=\beta_i(t)e_i$. Conjugation acts on the tensor quotient: it preserves brackets, and on invariant derivations the identity $(CDC^{-1})^p=CD^pC^{-1}$ preserves the restricted relations. This identity works over $R$ as well. Multiplication therefore gives $t e^a=(\sum_i a_i\beta_i)(t)e^a$ in $A\otimes_FR$. In particular these are character weights, not differentiated characters.

source.place: Theorem 10.40, p.207; root conjugation identity (135), 21.19, p.431; functoriality by conjugating invariant derivations.

proof.text: Put $D=N(p-1)$ and $P_d=\operatorname{span}_F\{e^a:0\leq a_i<p,\ |a|\leq d\}$, with $P_d=0$ for $d<0$. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-monomial-straightening] with $y_i=e_i$ and $q=p$. Its bounded-basis hypothesis is step 2. Its other hypotheses hold since $e_je_i-e_ie_j=[e_j,e_i]$ and $e_i^p=e_i^{[p]}$ lie in the span of the $e_i$. It gives the degree bound and both leading-product formulas. Since the sole bounded monomial of degree $D$ is $z$, the basis also gives $A=P_D$ and $L(P_{D-1})=0$.

source.place: Degree tracking in the reordering of 10.36 and restricted reduction of 10.40, pp.200--207.

proof.text: Write a nonzero $v\in A$ as $\sum_c v_c e^c$. Choose an exponent $a$ of maximal total degree $d$ with $v_a\ne0$, and put $b_i=p-1-a_i$, so $|b|=D-d$. For $|c|<d$, the degree bound in step 3 puts both $e^ce^b$ and $e^be^c$ in $P_{D-1}$. If $|c|=d$, their leading terms are given by that step. An overflow in $c+b$ puts both products in $P_{D-1}$. Otherwise $c+b$ is bounded and has degree $D$, forcing every entry to equal $p-1$, hence $c=a$. For $c=a$, each product is $z$ modulo $P_{D-1}$. Consequently $L(ve^b)=v_a=L(e^bv)\ne0$. This proves nondegeneracy in each argument without assuming the multiplication is commutative or the pairing symmetric.

source.place: Corollary 1.3(ii), p.149; the complementary-exponent calculation spelling out the filtered-to-graded argument.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] for this same Borel pair to choose a regular cocharacter $\lambda$ with $B=P(\lambda)$. Its Lie-weight formula says $h_i=\langle\beta_i,\lambda\rangle>0$ for every positive root. If a bounded exponent $a$ has $\sum_i a_i\beta_i=\tau$, pairing the difference with $\lambda$ gives $\sum_i(p-1-a_i)h_i=0$. All summands are nonnegative integers and each $h_i>0$, so every $a_i=p-1$. To identify weight spaces, use the universal point of $T$ over $F[T]$. For a vector $v=\sum_a v_a e^a$ of character weight $\gamma$, comparison of its coordinates in the scalar-extended basis gives $v_a(\chi_a-\gamma)=0$ in $F[T]$, where $\chi_a=\sum_i a_i\beta_i$. Whenever $v_a\ne0$, its invertibility as a scalar forces equality of the two character functions. Thus a weight space is spanned by precisely the basis vectors of that character. The preceding integer calculation gives $A_\tau=Fz$, and a vector in any other weight space has zero $z$ coefficient, so $L$ vanishes there.

source.place: Theorem 21.32 and Definition 21.35, pp.434--435; positive-character height applied to the PBW weights.

proof.text: If $N=0$, step 1 gives $U=1$ and $\mathfrak u=0$, while step 2 gives the single basis element $1$. Hence $A=F$, $z=1$ and $L=\operatorname{id}_F$. Its product pairing is nondegenerate since $L(v\cdot1)=v=L(1\cdot v)$, and the only weight is $\tau=0$. This also verifies directly the negative-filtration-index convention $P_{-1}=0$ used above.

source.place: Empty-root instance of Theorem 21.68(a) and empty-basis instance of Theorem 10.40.

Steps: step 1 gets the basis e_i from the root-product isomorphism (any enumeration, each U_beta inside U) and the restricted structure from restricted-rational-differentiation, which defines D_{x^[p]}=D_x^p, the same operation as the item. Step 2: the hypotheses of restricted-pbw-basis hold. The weights come from the conjugation formula on dual numbers over any R and are characters, not differentials. Step 3: brackets and e_i^p=e_i^[p] lie in W, and z is the only bounded monomial of degree D. Step 4: I recomputed the complementary-exponent argument, L(v e^b)=v_a=L(e^b v), which proves nondegeneracy on both sides without commutativity; it is genuinely elementary. Step 5: the regular cocharacter with B=P(lambda) gives <beta_i,lambda>>0; comparing coordinates at the universal point of T gives A_tau=Fz. Step 6: N=0 holds. New node: statement-only, inline definitions, true by Milne's p.200 inversion induction plus reduction of y^q (q>=2). I tested n=0, q=2 with y^2=y and with y^2=0, and a scalar commutator. It is strictly smaller than the item, generic, and not a clause of the item. A DAG grep (PBW, enveloping, straighten, normal order, monomial) found no duplicate: restricted-pbw-basis has no degree control and rational-pbw is the characteristic-0 unbounded case. Sources checked: Milne 10.36 (pp.200-201), 10.40 (p.207) and 21.68 (p.445). Mathieu is WANTED and the proof does not rely on it.
